Date of filing : 03.12.2018  Final arguments heard : 03.10.2024  Date of Award : 03.10.2024 ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 729/2018; Alisha & Anr. v. Ishtkar & Ors. Page 1 of 12  JUDGMENT 1.
By this judgment, I shall decide the present DAR (Detailed Accident Report) case, filed in respect of the fatal injury received by the deceased Zeeshan in a motor vehicular accident.
The DAR has been treated as claim petition under Section 166(4) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 on behalf of the petitioners/ legal heirs of the deceased.

2. Important facts of the case as per claim petition are that on 27.10.2018 at about 10:10 p.m., the deceased Zeeshan was crossing the main road at New Jafrabad Pulia, under Jafrabad Metro Station,

1 Jafrabad, Delhi.

In the meanwhile, a Wagon-R taxi bearing registration no.DL1RTA-9892 (in short "offending vehicle"), being driven by respondent no.1 Ishtkar from Seelampur towards Maujpur side at a high speed, rashly and negligently, came and hit the deceased with a great force.
Due to the forceful impact, the deceased fell down on road and got badly injured.
The driver/ respondent no.1 Ishtkar, who was fleeing after causing the accident, was chased and caught by one Mohd. Salman and was handed over to police.
The injured was removed to JPC Hospital, where he was declared brought dead.
In connection with the accident, FIR no.633/2016, under section 279/304-A IPC was registered at PS Jafrabad.
After completion of the investigation, charge-sheet was filed before the concerned court and the instant DAR was filed before this Tribunal for the grant of compensation to the claimants.
3. All the respondents appeared and filed their replies to the DAR/ claim petition.

_ 4. Respondent no.1, the driver in his written statement stated that the accident was caused due to negligence of the deceased himself, who was crossing the road by jumping the divider without seeing here and there and there was no zebra crossing on road.

Further, it is stated that the respondent no.1 was having a valid driving license and the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3 and therefore, liability to pay the compensation shall be of insurance company.
5. Respondent no.2, the registered owner in his written statement stated that he has nothing to do with the present case as he had already sold the alleged offending vehicle to respondent no.1 on 06.07.2018.
6. Respondent no.3/ insurance company in its written statement contended that as per part-III of DAR, driver/ respondent no.1 was driving the taxi but he was carrying the learning license only.
Rest, it took the general defences.
7.

Upon completion of pleadings of the parties, vide order dated 30.01.2020, following issues were framed:
1.

Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle no.DL-1RTA-9892 on 27.10.2018 at about 10:10 p.m., at Main Road, Near Jafrabad Metro Station, within the jurisdiction of PS Jafrabad, in rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh. Zeeshan?
OPP 2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
OPP 3. Relief.

In order to establish the claim, petitioners got examined five witnesses, as under:
i).

PW1 Irfan, elder brother of deceased Zeeshan deposed on the strength of his affidavit Ex.PW1/1 regarding the manner of accident, age and income of deceased and about the minor children/ legal heirs of the deceased and relied upon the following documents:-
a) Copy of Aadhaar Card of deceased Zeeshan as Ex.PW1/A (OSR).

f) Copy of Aadhaar Card of Mohd. Faiz, minor son of deceased as Ex.PW1/F (OSR).
g) Original Death Certificate of Noor Hasan, father of deceased as Ex.PW1/G.
ii).
PW2 Mohd. Salman was got examined as eye-witness of the accident.
In support o f h i s i d e n t i t y , h e p r o d u c e d a c o p y o f h i s ______________________________________________________________________ Driving License as Ex.PW1/A.
9 . On the other hand, no evidence was led by the respondents.

On the submission of learned counsel for respondent no.1 and 2 that he did not wish to lead any evidence, evidence of respondent no.1 and 2 was closed vide order dated 03.08.2024, whereas, evidence of respondent no.3 was closed vide detailed order of this Tribunal passed on 06.07.2024.
10.
Today on 03.10.2024, the respondent no.1/driver Ishtkar has been examined by the Tribunal under section 168 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam.

To the query as to how the accident had happened, the respondent no.1 stated that the deceased had jumped the divider and came in front of his van/ offending vehicle and that the deceased was trying to cross the road running from the portion of the road where there was no provision of crossing the road i.e., there was no zebra crossing.
The respondent no.1 also stated that he was driving the offending vehicle at the speed of about 20-25 kmph.
With the permission of the Tribunal, the respondent no.1 was cross-

examined by the learned counsel for the petitioner who inter-alia gave the suggestion that at the time of the accident, the speed of the offending vehicle was about 60-70 kmph which was denied by the respondent no.1.

sentences.text: I heard the final arguments advanced by learned counsels for the parties.
I also perused the evidence and other materials placed on record.

Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle no.DL- 1RTA-9892 on 27.10.2018 at about 10:10 p.m., at Main Road, Near Jafrabad Metro Station, within the jurisdiction of PS Jafrabad, in rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh. Zeeshan? OPP 12.
It is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
13.

sentences.text: 'Negligence' is failure to take proper care which a reasonable man would have taken under the circumstances.
What amounts to negligence depends on the facts of each particular case.
It may consist in omitting to do something which ought to be done or in doing something which ought to be done either in a different manner or not at all.
Where there is no duty to exercise care, negligence in t h e p o p u l a r s e n s e h a s n o l e g a l c o n s e q u e n c e . W h e r e t h e r e i s a d u t y t o

______________________________________________________________________ exercise care, reasonable care must be taken to avoid acts or omissions which can be reasonably foreseen to be likely to cause physical injury to persons or property.

The degree of care required in the particular case depends on the surrounding circumstances, and may vary according to the amount of the risk to be encountered and to the magnitude of the prospective injury.

The duty of care is owed only to those persons who are in the area of foreseeable danger; the fact that the act of the defendant violated his duty of care to a third person does not enable the plaintiff who is also injured by the same act to claim unless he is also within the area of foreseeable danger.
The same act or omission may accordingly in some circumstances involve liability as being negligent, although in other circumstances it will not do so.

The material considerations are the absence of care which is on the part of the defendant owed to the plaintiff in the circumstances of the case and damage suffered by the plaintiff, together with a demonstrable relation of cause and effect between the two.

14. Negligence is conduct which falls below the standard established for the protection of others against unreasonable risk of harm, this standard of conduct is ordinarily measured by what the reasonable man of ordinary prudence would do under the circumstances.

In order to objectify the law's abstractions like "care", "reasonableness" or "foreseeability" the man of ordinary prudence was invented as a model of the standard of conduct to which all men are required to conform.

sentences.text: "Reckless" means "careless", regardless or heedless of the possible harmful consequences of one's acts.

It presupposes that if thought was given to the matter by the doer before the act was done, it would have been apparent to him that there was a real risk of its having the relevant harmful consequences; but, granted this, recklessness covers a whole range of states of mind from failing to give any thought at all to whether or not there is any risk of those harmful consequences,
to recognising the existence of the risk and nevertheless deciding to ignore it.

[Ref: Naresh Giri v.
State of M.P., (2008) 1 SCC 791]

sentences.text: 16. If the statement is made that 'A' drove his car rashly and negligently, the said statement is not capable of objective verification by the Court or Tribunal as what is rash or negligence is an inference and a matter of opinion.
[Ref: Dias Jurisprudence, 5th Ed. p. 8].

For the objective verification by the Court or Tribunal, if 'A' was driving his car rashly and negligently, facts required to be proved on the basis of which the Court/Tribunal could reach to the inference and form an opinion that he was driving his car rashly and negligently.

The Tribunal is consciously not going into the nitty-gritty of the concept that one cannot be rash and negligent at the same time that is, if one is rash then one cannot be negligent at the same time and if one is negligent one cannot be rash at the same time; the presence of either rash or negligence negates the other.
17. Now coming to the issue, the testimony of the eye-witness PW2 Mohd. Salman is relevant to be discussed here.

PW2 deposed that the incident occurred on 27.10.018 at about 10:10 p.m., when he w a s ______________________________________________________________________ going towards Maujpur, a Wagon-R taxi bearing no. DL1RTA-9892, being driven in wrong and negligent manner, hit the deceased, who was crossing the Main Raod at Jafrabad Pulia, Metro Station Jafrabad, due to which deceased fell down on the road and became unconscious and was declared brought dead by the doctor in the hospital.
18. What PW2 with his statement that offending vehicle was driven in the wrong and negligent manner meant only he might be knowing as it was his inference an opinion.

Again, when he deposed that the deceased was hit while crossing the road due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle only PW2 might be knowing how and in what manner the offending vehicle was being driven rashly and negligently as at best the offending vehicle was being driven rashly and negligently was the opinion of PW2 with which the other persons including this Tribunal may or may not concur if the Tribunal has before it other facts for which inference could be drawn regarding the rashness and negligence of the respondent no.1 in driving the offending vehicle.
19. In the cross-examination of PW2, he deposed that the speed of the offending vehicle was about 100 kmph.

Without going into the question as to on what basis PW2 came to know that the speed of the offending vehicle was 100 kmph assuming that the offending vehicle was being driven at that speed then coming to the site plan which is at page no.18 of DAR, it was a straight road divided by the divider, which as per the respondent no.2 was of the height of about two feet ______________________________________________________________________

sentences.text: 5 and the divider did not have bushes, which means had the deceased cared to look in the direction of the traffic before crossing the road, the deceased would have been in a position to spot the offending vehicle from quite a distance as the speed of offending vehicle as per PW2 was about 100 kmph.

The fact that the accident happened at point A in the site plan which is very adjacent to the divider,
indicates that the deceased did not check for the oncoming traffic before stepping his foot on the road.
The manner of accident probablises the stand of the respondent no.1 that the deceased jumped the divider without looking here and there.

20. The site plan does not reveal that near about the spot of accident, there was any zebra crossing or any blinker to warn the driver of the vehicles and pedestrians may cross the road from that particular spot.

If motor vehicles be a beast which an owner/driver keeps at his peril then a person who does not follow basic precautions before crossing the road from a place which is not demarcated for crossing the road without looking left and right, does so at his own peril too.

If the people were allowed to cross the road from anywhere then there would have been no purpose of putting the zebra crossing over the road or the mandate of the law to stop before the zebra crossing over the red light.

21. The petitioner/ legal heirs of the deceased would be entitled to receive compensation only if on the balance of probability, it could have been proved that the respondent no.1 was rash/ negligent in d r i v i n g t h e o f f e n d i n g v e h i c l e . T h e r e s p o n d e n t n o . 1 a l s o h a s t o p r o v e ______________________________________________________________________ his defences on the balance of probability itself.
The burden of proof in the case of the respondents cannot be to prove the defences beyond reasonable doubt.

In the facts and circumstances of the case on the basis of deposition of the eyewitness PW2, the fact which has been proved is that the speed of the offending vehicle was about 100 kmph and that there was no zebra crossing from where the deceased was crossing the road.

These two facts have already been discussed herein above and in the opinion of the Tribunal, the same are not sufficient enough to pin the respondent no.1 either being rash or negligent in causing the accident in which the deceased lost his life.

As discussed above,
since the deceased lost his life because of his own rash and negligent act i.e. not looking right and left before crossing the road, therefore, the respondent no.1 cannot be held legally liable for causing the death of the deceased.
22. In the light of discussion herein above, the issue no.1 is decided against the petitioners and in favour of the respondents.
ISSUE NO.2 Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
As the issue no.1 has been decided against the petitioners, the petitioners are not entitled for any compensation.
Accordingly, issue no.2 is decided against the petitioners and in favour of the respondents.

24. As both the substantive issues have been decided against the petitioners, the petitioners are not e n t i t l e d

25.
The DAR/ claim petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
